title: GraphRAG & AI
summary: Cross-cutting hybrid GraphRAG engine (semantic retrieval + weighted graph traversal) letting the AI answer multi-hop questions with cited nodes/paths, suggest missing links, all local-first.
scope: Hybrid GraphRAG engine (Qdrant semantic + MySQL weighted graph traversal)
Cited answers (nodes + path + weights + chunk), anti-hallucination 'non so' threshold
Link prediction with human curation queue
Feedback loop and immutable weight recalculation
Graph node types: Chunk, Query, Answer, Citation, Path, Community, Suggested Link, Concept/Term, Embedding Anchor
Relation types: rappresenta, ancora_a, attraversa, cita, ha_generato, valutata_come, suggerisce, appartiene_a_comunita, sinonimo_di/definisce, simile_a
Edge weight factors: semantic similarity, useful-traversal frequency, human validation, suggestion confidence, source authority/freshness, answer feedback, temporal decay, node centrality

MVP features: GraphRAG orchestrator, query understanding, entity linking, weighted MySQL traversal, RRF fusion, permission filter, cited generation, 'don't know' model, ask/expand/path/subgraph APIs, base link prediction + curation queue, answer-centered graph visualization, feedback-driven weight recalc, bilingual enums

Data connectors/internal sources: domain nodes/edges (core + verticals), chunk/node embeddings via DocumentIngestionPipelineService->Qdrant, MySQL metadata/provenance, glossary/ontology, conversation history (llm), user feedback, domain events (SpringDomainEventPublisher); extension points: pluggable PF4J retrieval strategies, MCP graph tools, incremental embedding sync

Modules: knowledge, llm/LlmGatewayService, Qdrant vectorstore, MySQL/Flyway, document pipeline, agent, mcp, auth/LocalAuthFilter, automation, common, messaging, marketplace/PF4J, chat/SSE, Angular frontend
notes: Cross-cutting/transversal domain (the core AI engine) likely already covered by existing roadmap phases 1-7, not a standalone vertical. Classified PRD: dominant structure is product/feature-oriented (personas, 'Requisiti in input', MVP feature tables, KPI & success metrics, goals/value). SPEC competed strongly due to detailed graph data model (node/relation types, weight criteria) and API endpoint list; PRD chosen because the technical model serves to scope the feature rather than define binding contracts. No frontmatter, no filename convention, prose-heavy guide ('guida agli sviluppi LocalMind').
